lesson.text: Quick memory: what were the first wheels used for, over 5,000 years ago? (Shaping clay, on a potter's wheel.) Today: building a vehicle whose wheels roll straight.
A model vehicle has a chassis (its frame), axles (rods the wheels turn on) and wheels. Axle holders, like short tubes or straws, fix the axles to the chassis.
A fixed axle: the wheels are fixed to the axle, and the whole axle turns inside its holders. A free axle: the axle is fixed, and the wheels spin on it. Both work.
To roll straight, the axles must be parallel to each other and at right angles to the chassis. A crooked axle makes the car turn and wobble.
Wheels must be round and the same size, with the hole in the very middle. Leave a small gap so a wheel does not rub on the chassis: rubbing is friction, which slows it down.
Each turn, a wheel rolls as far as the distance round its edge. A wheel 30 cm round rolls 30 cm each turn, so 4 turns roll 4 × 30 = 120 cm.
Test it fairly: roll it down the same ramp, from the same height, and measure how far it goes. Change only one thing, like the size of the wheels, and test again.
Try it in the world: build a cart with 4 wheels on 2 axles, and a ramp to roll it down. For real: make a car from card, straws and bottle tops, and see how far it rolls.

exercises.hint: Look at the labels in the picture.
choices: the frame the axles fix to
the rod a wheel turns on
exercises.explain: The chassis is the vehicle's frame; the axles and wheels fix to it.

exercises.hint: It goes through the middle of the wheels.
choices: the rod that the wheels turn on
exercises.explain: An axle is the rod the wheels turn on.

exercises.prompt: A wheel needs its hole in the very middle to roll smoothly.
exercises.hint: What happens if the hole is near the edge?
exercises.explain: True: with the hole off-centre, the wheel bumps up and down as it turns.

exercises.hint: Look for the axle that is not at right angles to the chassis.
exercises.explain: The axle on the right is crooked, so this car would turn and wobble.

exercises.prompt: This car's axles are parallel, so it can roll straight.
exercises.hint: Are the axles at right angles to the chassis?
exercises.explain: True: both axles are parallel and at right angles to the chassis.

exercises.prompt: Match each part to its job.
matches: the rod the wheels turn on
fixes the axle to the chassis
exercises.hint: Think of the picture with the labels.
exercises.explain: Chassis: holds it together. Axle: the wheels turn on it. Axle holder: fixes the axle on. Wheel: rolls.

exercises.prompt: What is the difference between a fixed axle and a free axle?
exercises.hint: In one, the wheels and axle turn together.
choices: fixed: the axle turns; free: only wheels spin
a fixed axle cannot move at all
a free axle has no wheels
exercises.explain: On a fixed axle, the wheels and axle turn together inside the holders. On a free axle, only the wheels spin.

exercises.prompt: A wheel is 25 cm round its edge. How far does the car roll in 4 turns?
exercises.hint: Each turn rolls the distance round the wheel: multiply.

exercises.prompt: A wheel rubs on the side of the chassis. What happens?
exercises.explain: Rubbing is friction, which slows the car down. Leave a small gap between the wheel and the chassis.

exercises.prompt: This car rolls in a curve. Why?
exercises.hint: Look closely at the size of each wheel.
choices: one wheel is smaller than the others
exercises.explain: One wheel is smaller, so that side rolls less far each turn, and the car curves.

exercises.prompt: A wheel is 40 cm round. How many turns does it make to roll 200 cm?
exercises.hint: How many lots of 40 cm make 200 cm?

exercises.prompt: Put a fair ramp test in order.
exercises.hint: Set everything up before you let go.
items: let go of the car without pushing
set the ramp to one height
change one thing, then test again
exercises.explain: Set the ramp, let go without pushing, measure, repeat 3 times, then change one thing and test again.

exercises.prompt: To test fairly, change the ramp height and the wheels at the same time.
exercises.hint: How would you know which change made the difference?
exercises.explain: False: change only one thing at a time, so you know what made the difference.

exercises.prompt: Why are axles put at right angles to the chassis?
exercises.hint: Which way do the wheels roll when the axle is square?
choices: so the wheels point straight ahead
exercises.explain: At right angles, the wheels point straight ahead, so the car rolls straight.

exercises.prompt: A big wheel is 50 cm round and a small wheel 30 cm round. Each turns 3 times. How much further does the big one roll, in centimetres?
exercises.hint: Work out how far each rolls, then find the difference.

play.hook: The cart at the bottom of the ramp keeps wobbling. Find out how to make it roll straight!
coach: Axles are the rods the wheels turn on.
Parallel axles make a vehicle roll straight.
Rubbing is friction, and it slows a wheel down.
Each turn, a wheel rolls the distance round its edge.
A fair test changes only one thing.
play.world_task: Build a cart with 4 wheels on 2 axles, and a ramp to roll it down. How far does it go?
